cards.explanation: The answer is to return it to your brother. Moses, Israel's leader, says, “If you see your brother’s ox or sheep straying, you must not ignore it; be sure to return it to your brother.” (Deuteronomy 22:1) No pretending you didn't see it, no checking your pockets for something to do. I sat in the back of a junk drawer for years, so believe me, a neighbor who stops is a beautiful thing.

The answer is to take it home until he comes for it. Moses says that if your brother lives far off or you don't know who he is, the animal goes home with you and stays until he comes seeking it. Then you return it to him (Deuteronomy 22:2). Surprise, friends, you've got a houseguest with hooves! Not a bad deal for a stray, I think.

The answer is True! Moses says to do the same for his donkey, his cloak, “…or anything your brother has lost and you have found.” (Deuteronomy 22:3) That's a wide net, friends. Found a jacket on the road? It's his, not yours. And Moses adds, “…you must not ignore it…”

The answer is False. Waiting around isn't an option here. Moses says, “…you must not ignore it; you must help him lift it up.” (Deuteronomy 22:4) So you don't stand there watching a fallen ox and hoping for the best, friends. You get your hands on it and help your brother.

The answer is that he sees it as detestable to Him. Moses says whoever does these things “…is detestable to the LORD your God.” (Deuteronomy 22:5) That's the exact word the text uses, friends. I won't add anything to it, because the text doesn't.

The answer is that you may prolong your days. Moses says to let the mother go “…so that it may be well with you and that you may prolong your days.” (Deuteronomy 22:7) A promise of long life attached to a little bird, friends. I won't guess at the how, because the text doesn't say.

The answer is bloodguilt. Moses says to build the railing “…so that you do not bring bloodguilt on your house if someone falls from it.” (Deuteronomy 22:8) A railing costs a lot less than a regret, friends. Build it before anybody has to find out why.

The answer is her father and mother. When a husband has accused his wife of shameful conduct, Moses says “…the young woman’s father and mother shall bring the proof of her virginity to the city elders at the gate” (Deuteronomy 22:15). Both parents speak up for their daughter before the elders. The husband has accused her, and her parents answer him.

The answer is that they punish him and fine him. When the cloth shows the husband's accusation is false, the elders “…shall take the man and punish him.” and they fine him a hundred shekels of silver, which goes to the young woman's father. (Deuteronomy 22:18-19) The text says he gave “…a virgin of Israel a bad name.” His accusation costs him.

The answer is False. Moses says that after the false accusation, she “…shall remain his wife; he must not divorce her as long as he lives.” (Deuteronomy 22:19) So the husband can't just walk away from the marriage.

The answer is False. When a man is found lying with another man's wife, Moses says, “…both the man who slept with her and the woman must die.” (Deuteronomy 22:22) The man and the woman are named together. It's a heavy law, and the text is clear on it.

The answer is that she did not cry out in the city. Moses says both are stoned, “…the young woman because she did not cry out in the city, and the man because he has violated his neighbor’s wife.” (Deuteronomy 22:24) This is a heavy one, friends. Two people, two reasons, and Moses gives each reason plainly.

The answer is True. In the open country, Moses says, “…only the man who has done this must die.” (Deuteronomy 22:25) Then he says, “Do nothing to the young woman, because she has committed no sin worthy of death.” (Deuteronomy 22:26) The text is clear about where the blame lies.

The answer is neighbor. Moses says, “This case is just like one in which a man attacks his neighbor and murders him.” (Deuteronomy 22:26) He sets it right beside murder. The woman cried out, and the verse says there was no one to save her (Deuteronomy 22:27). This one is heavy.

The answer is that he must marry her and never divorce her. Along with the fifty shekels of silver, Moses says “…she must become his wife because he has violated her. He must not divorce her as long as he lives.” (Deuteronomy 22:29) Two requirements, friends, and both are in that one verse.

The answer is his father's wife. Moses says, “A man is not to marry his father’s wife, so that he will not dishonor his father’s marriage bed.” (Deuteronomy 22:30) That's the closing law of the chapter, friends, and it's about keeping a family's marriage bed honored.
